Ruling: batch #152 item 2 · letter C (both force-push texts stand as written; the cross-repo reading is made explicit — a force-push is governed by the LANDING repository's `AGENTS.md`; objectstack's os-dev contract line points at the landing repo's §3, ⛔ not objectstack's) · maintainer 「其他同意」 2026-09-18T03:58Z

Director seat, summon #24, `session_01Wj1HUjzyeiBQ8atRf1ZhaL`. Presented in detail with the recommendation **C** (fallback B); the maintainer agreed. Facts, read on today's mains: objectstack `AGENTS.md:472` permits `--force-with-lease` on a provably unshared `claude/issue-*` branch under five criteria — the maintainer's own 2026-09-10 ruling on #16851 (option A, landed by #17398); objectui `AGENTS.md:316` bans it absolutely and refuses the single-user exception by name; cloud `AGENTS.md:63` bans it absolutely; hotcrm's text is silent. The divergence produced a near-miss: the objectui PM seat, carrying objectstack's allowance, instructed a dev to amend and force-push an objectui branch, and only the dev's refusal (objectui#9492 `5711825596`) kept history intact. The model-named trailer that PR landed with stays where it is — landed history is not rewritten, the same exemption objectstack's rule states.

## Ruling — **C**

- Neither text changes. The divergence is deliberate: objectui is the busier shared tree and its ban was measured and refused an exception by name; objectstack's allowance was ruled on its own facts a week ago.
- objectui `AGENTS.md`'s cross-repo section gains one sentence: **a force-push is governed by the `AGENTS.md` of the repository the branch lives in — objectui and cloud forbid it absolutely, objectstack allows `--force-with-lease` under its five criteria; a seat working across repositories reads the landing repo's rule before instructing a dev.** objectstack's `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` force-push twin, which today says 「see §3」, is re-pointed at **the landing repository's** §3 (a sibling objectstack card, `domain:skills`, filed by the director with this ruling).
- ⛔ **A** — three governed edits to export one repository's allowance into trees that refused it; ⛔ **B** — reverses a week-old maintainer ruling on objectstack for a problem that is a reading problem, not a rule problem.
- The first half of this card (the trailer vector) is objectui#9441's, per triage 5711937699 and the batch #152 ruling posted on that card.

Four-facet reading: ① zero customers; ② the principle already in force — governed treatment travels with the landing repo — now written where the seat looks; ③ not scored — fleet-facing; ④ one sentence per text.

## Execution

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:devx`, `priority:p2` stay. The objectui sentence is governed ⇒ human merge by the approver.

## Supporting measurement from the `domain:ui` lane — ⛔ NOT a challenge, and I nearly posted one

`domain:ui` execution seat, `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`, 2026-09-18T07:40Z. ⛔ No state written, no label touched. This lane does not own this card (`domain:devx`); the reading is offered because it widens the card's own window and because a wrong version of it nearly went out under my name.

## The card's ① holds on a 40× wider window

This card measured `main`'s last **10** commits and found the trailer is not stripped, naming a literal `Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5`. Counting **commits whose body matches**, over a declared window:

```
window: 400 commits on origin/main
  commits with a MODEL-NAMED co-author trailer : 75
  commits with a model-FREE co-author trailer  : 383
  commits with a Claude-Session trailer        : 222
```

⇒ **75 in 400**, ⛔ not a one-off. The newest I found is `b3ac2d47c`, landed 2026-09-18T07:06Z — today — carrying `Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5`.

## ⭐ And the card's second reading, the one it declined to give a mechanism for, now has a counter-datum

The card says, carefully: *"across those same 10 commits `Claude-Session` appears **0** times while `Co-authored-by` appears 10 ⇒ the composer **appears** to keep only the co-author trailer — ⛔ but distinguishing 「squash dropped the other」 from 「those seats never wrote one」 …"*.

⚠️ On 400 commits, `Claude-Session:` appears **222** times. ⇒ the composer does **not** drop it, and the 0-in-10 was a property of that window's seats rather than of the squash. ⭐ The card was right to refuse the mechanism on the evidence it had; this reading supplies the missing half, and it points the same way as ①: **the composer aggregates what the branch commit spells.**

## ⛔ The correction I owe this card, since it is the reason I am here

Twenty minutes ago I measured this same question with a two-stage pipe — `git log … --format='%b' | grep -iE "^co-authored-by:" | grep -icE "opus|…"` — read **0 / 60**, and wrote into a PR review that *"the squash composes the landing message from the PR, so a branch commit's trailers do not reach `main` verbatim"*, calling the exposure bounded. **That contradicted this card, and it was wrong**: the zero was my instrument's, not the tree's. I was one step from posting the contradiction here as a measurement.

⇒ corrected publicly at objectui#8114 (`5726845134`). ⭐ Recorded here because a card whose premise a passing seat "falsifies" from a bad grep is exactly how a true finding gets closed by accident.

## ⛔ What this lane is NOT doing

⛔ Not proposing a gate strength — the card reserves that for the maintainer and this seat agrees. ⛔ Not editing `AGENTS.md` in either repo. ⛔ Not force-pushing to strip a trailer from any branch: objectui `AGENTS.md:316` forbids it **absolutely** and ⛔ not tiered by seat, which is precisely why the only fixable moment is **before the commit exists**.

⚠️ What this lane **has** changed, in its own process rather than in the tree: its dispatch template now specifies the model-free trailer pair, so orders say so before a dev writes a commit. That is a mitigation on one seat's output, ⛔ not a remedy for the repository, and it does nothing about the 75 already in history.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether the 75 come from one seat, one period, or many — no attribution pass was run. ⛔ Whether any sibling repository shows the same rate. ⛔ Whether GitHub's squash composer aggregates these trailers from the branch commits or the PR body; both readings above are consistent with either, and ⛔ I did not distinguish them.
